what.text: A requirement is something the system must do, or a property it must have.

levels.text: Business requirements state high-level goals. Stakeholder requirements say what end users expect. Solution requirements describe the product, and they come in two kinds.

fr.text: Functional requirements describe behavior: what the system does. The student shall display his weekly schedule. The mailing service shall send a welcome email.

nfr.text: Nonfunctional requirements describe qualities and constraints: how well, and within which limits.

s1.text: No more than two level-one faults per month. That's reliability.

s2.text: Available ninety-eight percent of business hours. Availability.

s3.text: Six seconds or less, for five thousand users an hour. Performance.

s4.text: A password of at least eight characters, with one upper-case letter and one digit. Security.

s5.text: Runs on both Windows and Linux. Portability.

s6.text: Implemented in Java: a constraint. Talks to a bar code reader: an external interface. Locks the login page after three failed attempts: error handling.

test.text: So ask one question. Does it say what the system does? Functional. Does it say how well, or under which limits? Nonfunctional.

srs.text: All of them go into the Software Requirements Specification.
